title: Italian Game: the Blackburne Shilling trap
line: A pawn left out as bait: taking it walks into mate.

steps.text: Black's knight jumps forward a second time and leaves the pawn on e5 unguarded. This rare move is bait.
Taking the pawn is the first slip: the black queen comes out and attacks the knight and the pawn on g2.
Taking a second pawn loses at once: the queen takes on g2 and then on e4 with check, and the knight mates.
Back before the bait. Leave the pawn: take the knight that jumped forward.

wrong.f3e5: That takes the bait, a first slip. The queen comes out, and one more greedy capture walks into the mate you just saw.

also.e1g1: Castling also leaves the bait alone. This lesson takes the knight.

steps.after: Black has moved the same knight twice, and now it is gone.

steps.text: Castle. Your king leaves the center before anything can hit it there.
Put your rook behind the pawn on e4. Then the pawn can push forward and chase the knight.
steps.after: Your pieces are out and Black is still behind. Leaving the bait cost you nothing.

summary: A pawn left unguarded on purpose can be bait. Ask what the other side gets before you take it.
